earnings.title: Western Midstream Announces Third-Quarter 2026 Results
highlights: Reported third-quarter 2026 Net income attributable to limited partners of $324.8 million, generating quarterly Adjusted EBITDA (1) of $708.3 million, which represents a 12-percent increase compared to the prior-year period, and third-quarter Distributable Cash Flow (1) of $512.3 million.

Net income (loss) attributable to limited partners for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $324.8 million, or $0.78 per common unit (diluted), with third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (1) totaling $708.3 million and Distributable Cash Flow (1) totaling $512.3 million.
Reported third-quarter 2026 Cash flows provided by operating activities of $567.5 million, generating third-quarter Free Cash Flow (1) of $244.2 million.
Third-quarter 2026 Cash flows provided by operating activities totaled $567.5 million and third-quarter 2026 Free Cash Flow (1) totaled $244.2 million.
Third-quarter 2026 Free Cash Flow (1) after distributions totaled negative $148.5 million as a result of organic growth capital expenditures.

quotes.text: WES achieved record natural-gas throughput, partnership-wide and in the Delaware Basin, driven by increased throughput from our legacy assets and a full quarter of contribution from the Brazos Delaware acquisition that closed in June.

outlook: Reaffirming 2026 Adjusted EBITDA (2) , Distributable Cash Flow (2) , and Free Cash Flow (2) guidance ranges of $2.750 billion to $2.950 billion, $2.050 billion to $2.250 billion, and $1.100 billion to $1.300 billion, respectively.

Expect to be slightly above the high end of the 2026 total capital expenditures (3) guidance range of $850.0 million to $1.0 billion, driven by capital needs related to producers’ accelerating activity and WES’s investment in the Solitude Pipeline System.

items.heading: We are dependent on Occidental for over 50% of revenues related to the natural gas, crude oil, NGLs, and produced water that we gather, transport, recycle, treat, supply, and/or dispose. A material reduction in Occidental’s production that is gathered, treated, processed, or transported by our assets would result in a material decline in our revenues and cash available for distribution.
Occidental’s ownership of our general partner may result in conflicts of interest.
Any future credit-rating downgrade could negatively impact our cost of and ability to access capital.
Sustained low natural-gas, NGLs, or oil prices and volatility of such prices could adversely affect our business.

Because of the natural decline in production from existing wells, our success depends on our ability to compete for new sources of oil and natural-gas throughput, which is dependent on certain factors beyond our control. Any decrease in the volumes that we gather, process, treat, and transport could affect our business and operating results adversely.
Our profitability may be negatively impacted by inflation in the cost of labor, materials, and services.
